# MX vs llmx scalar NVFP4 path

Read-only source comparison, pinned MX commit `c4d12e2c0094c9028318bed5bb1a30bb48f8a35b`. No source was copied, and no build, run, or GPU work was done. MX references below are `git show` source paths at that commit; llmx shader references are the authoritative `a32f0ff7f` worktree (runtime build identity `bc845`). The padded `[32][65]` shader layout cited below is from this revision, not `57b14db94`.

## Source anchors

| Concern | MX c4d12e2 source | llmx source | Comparison |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tile configs | `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp:1806-1808` | `src/backends/vulkan/shaders/matmul_tile.comp:94-107` | MX no-coop quant tiles have K=32: medium is BLOCK128, BM64, BN64; large is BLOCK128, BM128, BN128. llmx uses 256 threads, 64x64 tile, K stage32. |
| Scalar thread-to-output map | `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/mul_mm.comp:239-261,351-362` | `src/backends/vulkan/shaders/matmul_tile.comp:92-97,471-500` | MX large config gives WNITER=4 and `sums[64]` of FLOAT_TYPEV2: 128 scalar accumulators per invocation for a 128x128 tile / 128-thread workgroup. MX medium is 32 scalar accumulators per invocation for 64x64 / 128 threads. llmx retained 64x64 / 256 threads gives 16 scalar accumulators per invocation; the K32/128 experiment gives 32. |
| Shared-memory layout | `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/mul_mm.comp:188-197`; `mul_mm_funcs.glsl:1-18` | `src/backends/vulkan/shaders/matmul_tile.comp:104-107` | MX stores K pairs as FLOAT_TYPEV2 in row-major A and B arrays with stride BK/2+1 (17 pairs for BK32). llmx stores scalar floats in K-major `[32][65]` A and B tiles. These layouts have different bank/access patterns and different per-lane reuse. |
| NVFP4 decode and vector load | `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/mul_mm_funcs.glsl:326-347`; format structs `types.glsl:1843-1869` | `src/backends/vulkan/shaders/matmul_tile.comp:240-254` | MX fallback float path selects one 16-value scale group, reads two packed bytes, decodes four codes, and writes two FLOAT_TYPEV2 pairs to shared memory. llmx reads paired nibbles and writes low/high values into scalar shared slots. Both apply scale before the shared tile. |
| Accumulation schedule | `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/mul_mm.comp:408-444`; `dot_product_funcs.glsl:1-25` | `src/backends/vulkan/shaders/matmul_tile.comp:471-500` | MX stages BK32, consumes K as 16 vector2 steps; dot_product is two ordered FMA operations unless the selected DOT2_F16 variant uses the mixed-float dot intrinsic. llmx consumes scalar K steps and does four scalar FMA operations per row for four output columns. The exact MX arithmetic variant depends on device feature and precision selection; source alone does not prove which ran. |
| Format pipeline setup | `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp:2633-2636,2737-2751` | `src/backends/vulkan/shaders/matmul_tile.comp:240-253` | In the non-coop branch MX registers NVFP4 x F32 scalar pipelines (with an optional f16 accumulator variant when `device->fp16` is true); the FP32-only fallback also registers NVFP4 x F32. The separate integer-dot pipeline list shown at `2643-2656` does not register NVFP4 x Q8_1, so a missing Q8_1 lookup falls back to the direct float-input pipeline. |
| Dispatch choice | `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp:2257-2273,2862-2871,4790-4791,5999-6005,6333-6376` | N/A | The generic selector chooses large when M,N exceed 64, but the AMD capability setup at 4790-4791 sets `mul_mat_l[type] = coopmat_support && driver != AMD proprietary`. For a MI50 path with `coopmat_support=false`, large is disabled before filtering; therefore the generic large choice does not apply. Assuming the NVFP4 medium config survives shared-memory filtering, the source-selected candidate is medium 64x64/128 threads. This is still dispatch inference, not an observed pipeline witness. |
| GFX906 tuning branch | `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp:1852-1860` | N/A | The AMD_GCN / non-proprietary override changes the integer-MMQ medium tile only. It does not override the direct NVFP4 x F32 scalar `tc_mmq` large tile. |

## Corrected load-layout hypothesis

The earlier tile-scaling proposal is superseded: the source comparison exposed a more direct remaining difference. MX's ordinary scalar path stages `FLOAT_TYPEV2` values; in its FP32 variant this is `vec2`, not half. The shared arrays are row-major in the output coordinate and pair-K coordinate: `a_shmem_index(m,k_pair)` maps to `m*SHMEM_STRIDE+k_pair`, with `SHMEM_STRIDE=BK/2+1` (MX `mul_mm.comp:188-197`, `mul_mm_funcs.glsl:1-18`). NVFP4 decoding writes two adjacent K values per pair (`mul_mm_funcs.glsl:326-347`). For BK32, the scalar compute loop takes 16 pair steps (`mul_mm.comp:408-444`). Its default F32 dot performs two scalar FMAs per pair (`dot_product_funcs.glsl:18-25`); the separate `DOT2_F16` branch is not evidence that a mixed-dot pipeline ran.

llmx keeps scalar floats in K-major `[32][65]` shared arrays (`matmul_tile.comp:104-107`). Each K step loads four adjacent output-column activations, then updates four accumulators per owned row (`matmul_tile.comp:471-482`). Thus MX groups adjacent K values in shared loads and compute, while llmx groups adjacent N outputs. This is a concrete layout/scheduling difference after accounting for thread count; it does not prove that MX's layout is faster or that its pipeline was active.

Best narrow discriminator: an NV-only experiment that keeps the 256-thread llmx ownership, F32 values, output tile and decode/scaling contract, but stages adjacent K pairs in row-major shared arrays and consumes each pair with two explicit FMAs in ascending K order (`k0`, then `k1`). Do not use DOT2 or half packing. This preserves llmx's per-output accumulation order while isolating pair-K staging/access from MX's arithmetic expression order. Check output identity, register/LDS stats, and matched repeated prefill/decode timings. The MI50 medium-candidate dispatch above is source-inferred only; no active MX pipeline is claimed.

## Paired-K candidate observation

The isolated paired-K candidate passed native checks and produced identical output hashes. In the before/after diagnostic ISA (`build-nvfp4-tile-probe/smoke-before/0-matmul_tile_nvfp4.txt` vs `paired-k-checks/smoke/0-matmul_tile_nvfp4.txt`), static `ds_read*` instruction count falls from 112 to 64 while `v_fmac_f32` remains 512 and barriers remain 2. The candidate uses `ds_read2_b64` to fetch two vec2 pair slots per instruction, and the compute stream still issues the same number of scalar FMAs; it changes how shared values are grouped/loaded, not the arithmetic count. Pipeline stats changed from 61 to 69 VGPR and 16896 to 17408 bytes LDS, with zero scratch in both. These are static shader/pipeline observations, not dynamic LDS transaction, bank-conflict, occupancy, or stall measurements.

The `tc*4+j` output-column ownership is retained, but the physical activation address changed from K-major scalar `xs[k][col]` (65-float K stride) to row-major `xs_pairs[col][pair]` (17 vec2 K-pair stride). Therefore the previous bank-address argument based on the old `[K][column]` stride does not carry over. For adjacent columns the new row-major base advances 17 vec2 slots (34 32-bit words), but lane-to-`tc` mapping and actual bank serialization are not proven by these listings; no same-bank claim should be made from the source formula alone. The matched operator ABBA showed modest mixed shape changes (1024x896: before .653/.641 ms, after .599/.505 ms; other shapes roughly 1-2% lower), insufficient to claim a durable win. A separate smoke reports .47152 ms, 69 VGPR, 17408 bytes LDS, zero scratch. Treat timings as recorded evidence, not a causal conclusion about the instruction reduction.

# MX NVFP4 dispatch witness status

Read-only inspection of the saved Qwen3.5-0.8B screen. No GPU, build, or benchmark was run for this check.

## What the saved artifacts pin

- Run receipt: `/zpool1/llmx-xdev-quant-20261020/nvfp4-20261025/perf-screen-v1/execution.json`. It pins MX source commit `c4d12e2c0094c9028318bed5bb1a30bb48f8a35b`, run container image `sha256:2787625f463391c440798579bac0d012c77fdfa949d086d036cdbd77f0b8d600`, and records the MX build receipt hash `23fd9af6bb49099659b7bfd6ef0b4482c3eaef3efe7042186aa32487642bf442`. The receipt explicitly says the reused MX libraries were built with a different image/toolchain than the screen container.
- MX source/build receipt: `/zpool1/llmx-xdev-quant-20261020/tq-pair-20261024/tq-existing-path-v1/clean-build-40101812090/arms/mx/build-result.json`; it pins the same MX revision and build image `sha256:e369e69469f20d3940d3689abdbcc33545a5db0361807119ef003b1beb759d85`. Its configure command uses `GGML_VULKAN=ON` and omits `GGML_VULKAN_DEBUG` (default OFF).
- The runtime executable was `/ref/bin/llama-bench` from the mounted `mx-build` directory; SHA256 `7c2420a363b3301183f40ccda8ff9cc0dc6176aaf076465fabbc6f217f6cdfd4`. Its Vulkan library SHA256 is `c653698268e4410f60fd2d64c9b46ef90dab9ec66964f4cfdb9c90331a9a6299`. The wrapper was `/wrapper/mx-cli-bench-vulkan`; the screen receipt pins its hash as `69d90973192d4958fbfcfd0f7833391e6b9b8c8f91f03a12233eb9644e839cdf`.
- The captured device line reports RADV MI50/MI60, `fp16: 1`, `fp4: 0`, and `matrix cores: none`. The model log confirms Qwen3.5-0.8B GGUF and 108 NVFP4 tensors. The wrapper command was `/wrapper/mx-cli-bench-vulkan /model.gguf 4 512 128 1`.

## Dispatch is not witnessed

The saved MX run log contains no `ggml_vk_dispatch_pipeline` or `ggml_vk_guess_matmul_pipeline` lines. It therefore does not establish whether the actual matmul used F32 scalar pairs, an F16-accumulator shader, or a cooperative-matrix shader, nor which tile was dispatched. `fp16: 1` only proves the device reports FP16 support. `matrix cores: none` is not a direct log of `coopmat_support`; the source's AMD capability setup disables the large tile when `coopmat_support` is false, but that source condition alone is not a pipeline witness. The benchmark wrapper also does not record per-op input type or precision.

Source-based candidate only: for a non-coopmat device, `ggml_vk_get_dequantize_mul_mat_mat` selects the NVFP4 `f16acc` variant when `device->fp16` is true and op precision is `GGML_PREC_DEFAULT` (`ggml-vulkan.cpp:7540-7570`); otherwise it selects `f32acc`. `ggml_vk_guess_matmul_pipeline` picks a size based on M/N and enabled flags (`8571+`), and the chosen `pipeline->name` is available at the dispatch point (`7967`). This does not prove those conditions held in the screen.

## Smallest diagnostic once resources are free

Rebuild the pinned MX source/runtime libraries in an isolated diagnostic tree using the original pinned build image/toolchain, adding `-DGGML_VULKAN_DEBUG=ON` to the existing CMake configure flags (`ggml/CMakeLists.txt:226`, `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/CMakeLists.txt:128-129`); retain the pinned wrapper. Run it inside the same screen container image on the same model/device. The existing `VK_LOG_DEBUG` at `ggml-vulkan.cpp:7967` then prints each dispatched `pipeline->name`; capture the NVFP4 matmul names and workgroup counts. Registered names encode input/kernel type (`matmul_nvfp4_f32`), accumulator variant (`_f16acc` or no suffix for `_f32acc`), and tile size (`_s`, `_m`, `_l`, optionally `_aligned_...`). To directly identify cooperative support and per-op precision, add one NVFP4-only diagnostic at the selection site near `ggml_vk_compute_forward_mul_mat` line 9042 that prints `src0->type`, `effective_src1_type`, `dst->op_params[0]`, dimensions, `pipeline->name`, and `coopmat_support`/`coopmat2`/`fp16`. This is diagnostic-only; do not set a precision override. Because the screen's MX library build image differs from the run image, the rebuilt diagnostic should be treated as a dispatch witness, not silently mixed into the old timing pair.
